name: downloadActivityFit
description:
Download the ORIGINAL .FIT file of an activity and save it on the user's computer.
Returns the absolute path of the saved .fit file (second-by-second HR, cadence, speed, laps).
The file is saved once in the fit folder of the data dir; a later call does not download it
again. Use it only when the user wants the file itself: getActivityLaps and getActivitySets
already read it.

name: editDashboard
description:
Changes the layout, the custom widgets or the languages of the dashboard page (a page from the
template; call writeDashboard first). Without arguments it only reads: the reply has the layout, the
custom widgets, the missing texts of each language, the catalogue of built-in widgets and `widgetApi`,
the guide to writing a custom widget. `layout` replaces the whole layout (the text of the page's
'Copy layout'); `place` adds widgets at the end of a board; `widgets` adds or replaces custom widgets
by id and saves them in the widget library (<data-dir>/widgets.json), which every page from the
template gets; `removeWidgets` removes them from this page and its boards, `forgetWidgets` also
from the library. `widgetTexts` adds texts to custom widgets by id, language and key, e.g.
{"longest-ride": {"de": {"title": "Längste Fahrt"}}}. `languages` adds page texts by key, e.g.
{"de": {"title": "Training + Erholung"}}: keys and {placeholders} as in `englishTexts: true`; a
text with "|" has a singular and a plural form. Missing texts show in English.
`removeLanguages` removes languages that `languages` added.

layout.description: A whole layout: { base, boards: { all: [{ id, widget, type?, span, hidden?, baseSpan? }] }, seen?: { all: [widget names] } }. `seen` is the record of the preset widgets that each board has met: give it back as you got it.

board.description: all, recovery, running, strengthTraining, walking, hiking, cycling, swimming, racket, generic (Other), or another SDK sport name

widget.description: A widget id of the catalogue or a custom widget

type.description: The type the widget shows, when not the board's

code.description: The body of a function (el, ctx): see widgetApi

texts.description: Texts by language code and key; title is the title: see widgetApi

removeWidgets.description: Ids of custom widgets to remove from this page

forgetWidgets.description: Ids of custom widgets to remove from the library and from this page

widgetTexts.description: Texts of custom widgets by widget id, language code and key

languages.description: Texts by language code and key

removeLanguages.description: Codes of added languages, e.g. de

englishTexts.description: Also return the English texts to translate

path.description: The .html file; relative paths are inside the data dir

name: garminGet
description:
Generic read-only GET on the Garmin Connect Personal API, for endpoints not covered by the
other tools or when a query parameter name has to be adjusted. 'path' is relative and starts
with '/', e.g. /fitnessage-service/fitnessage/v2/2026-10-25 . 'query' is an optional
URL query string without '?', e.g. date=2026-10-25&foo=bar .

name: getActivity
description:
Garmin's full JSON for one activity: summaryDTO (start time, distance in metres, duration and
movingDuration in seconds, averageSpeed in m/s, HR, calories, training effect and load,
intensity minutes, Body Battery change, sets and reps of a strength session), splitSummaries
(one total per split type, such as the run and walk segments), the activity type and
metadataDTO (device maker, lap count, personal record flag). Private ids are left out.
Use it for a field that listActivities does not give: listActivities gives the common fields
in km and min/km, for many activities in one call. It has no laps, sets or samples: use
getActivityLaps, getActivitySets or downloadActivityFit for them.

name: getActivityLaps
description:
Laps of an activity as recorded by the watch (manual laps, auto-lap every km, or workout
steps), read from the original .FIT file. One row per lap: distance (km), timer time,
pace (min/km, foot sports) or speed (km/h), average/max HR, cadence (spm for running),
ascent/descent, average power, running form (gctMs, vertRatioPct, vertOscCm, strideCm),
intensity (active, interval, rest, recovery, warmup, cooldown; the auto laps of a free run can
be interval), lap trigger, and the step of the planned workout (step: the reps of one drill
share it). A swim lap also has metres, swimPace (per 100 m), stroke, lengths, swolf and strokes.
Use it for intervals and per-km splits; getActivity does not have them.
For a run: split (pace of the first and second half, kind, hrDriftPct) and, for a structured
workout, work (reps, pace, avgHR, and the fade of each step with more than one rep, pct). For a
swim: sets, the laps in a row of one distance, stroke and intensity (reps, firstPace, lastPace, pct: above 0 is
slower, firstSwolf, lastSwolf). null is n/a.
For a run, plan is the planned workout that the watch ran (null without one): its name and,
per lap with a step in lap order, the step's target (type, low, high, unit; or zone), done (the
lap in that unit), verdict (hit inside the target, ends included, or miss) and off (how far
outside, in the unit: s/km for pace, above 0 is slower). An open or zone target, a target in
%max or %ftp, a target outside a plausible range, a lap under 15 m or 8 s or a lap without the
value has verdict null.

name: getActivitySets
description:
Strength training sets of an activity, read from the original .FIT file. One entry per
exercise, in the order first done, with its movement category, its primary and secondary
muscles (from Garmin's exercise catalogue) and its active sets: reps,
weight (kg, absent when none was recorded), set time in seconds and the rest after the set
(restSec). Each exercise with weight also has top (the heaviest set of 1 to 12 reps, then the
most reps; without one, the heaviest set) and e1rmKg (the best estimated 1RM, Epley, of its
sets of 1 to 12 reps; null when it has none). Exercise names are stable across sessions, so
they can be used for per-exercise trends. Edits made later in Garmin Connect (renamed
exercises, corrected reps or weights) are not in the .FIT file. Use it for strength sessions;
for runs, rides and swims use getActivityLaps.
plan is the planned workout that the watch ran (null without one): its name and, per planned
exercise and rep plan (a pyramid gives a row per rep plan) in plan order, plannedSets,
plannedReps (low to high; high null is at least low),
doneSets, reps, and verdict (hit or miss, why: sets or reps; extra and over count the done sets
above the plan and above the high end); a warm-up or cool-down row (part) and a notInPlan row
have verdict null. In a rest-pause group (a repeat of one exercise with a rest of 20 s or less
inside it and a longer rest after it), only the first set of each pass is judged on reps.
Each planned row also has plannedRestSec: the planned rests right after its sets,
in seconds and plan order (null: an open rest, ended with the lap button; empty: no
rest right after it, such as the first exercise of a superset).

name: getActivityWorkouts
description:
The planned workout that an activity followed, as created in Garmin Connect: its steps in
order, each with its intensity (warmup/active/rest/recovery/cooldown), its duration (time in
seconds, reps, or open), its target (cadence, heart rate, pace, or open, with low and high
values), the exercise for strength steps, and the coach's notes. A step with durationType
REPEAT_UNTIL_STEPS_CMPLT repeats the steps from stepIndex durationValue up to it, targetValue
times in all. Use it for the whole plan and its notes. For plan against done (hit or miss),
read the plan field of getActivitySets (strength) or getActivityLaps (runs) instead; a swim
has no plan field.
An empty list means the activity followed no planned workout. Null fields are left out.

name: getBodyBattery
description:
Body Battery for up to 14 days, yyyy-MM-dd: for each day how much it charged and drained,
its readings through the day as [timestamp, level] pairs, and the events that changed it
(sleep, activities, stress, naps) with their start, duration and impact, and Garmin's
feedback. Use it to see why Body Battery went up or down. For one number per day with steps
and stress use getDailySummary; for the change of one activity, listActivities.

name: getDailyHeartRate
description:
Heart rate of one day, yyyy-MM-dd: restingHeartRate, minHeartRate and maxHeartRate (bpm),
lastSevenDaysAvgRestingHeartRate, and heartRateValues, the samples of the day as [timestamp,
bpm] pairs (several hundred, so the answer is about 13 KB). Use it for the HR curve of a day.
For resting HR over several days use getDailySummary with fromDate and toDate; for the zone
limits use getHeartRateZones.

name: getDailySummary
description: Daily user summary (steps, calories, stress, body battery, resting HR) for one date, or for up to 14 days (fromDate and toDate; the range answer has Garmin's v2 field names), yyyy-MM-dd. Use it for the totals of each day; for sleep use getSleep, for the Body Battery events getBodyBattery, and for the HR samples getDailyHeartRate.

name: getDashboardData
description:
All the data of the training dashboard in one call: HR zones, fitness age, the activities of the
last `weeks` weeks (compact summaries, with strength sets and laps where they apply; a strength
session with sets also has `planVerdicts`: hit or miss for each exercise of the plan that the
watch ran, null without a plan; a run whose laps are read, or whose .FIT file is saved, has
`planVerdicts` too: hit or miss for each lap with a planned target), the activities of the
weeks before for the period comparison,
daily HRV, the last 14 days of sleep and daily
summaries (with `recoveryHistory`, also short rows of the older days: date, sleep hours, sleep
score and resting HR), and `units`: the measurement system of the Garmin profile (metric, statute_us or
statute_uk) that the page shows; the data itself is always metric; `locale`: the language of
the Garmin profile, e.g. it or pt-BR. Keeps a local cache and
fetches from Garmin only what is new since the last call, so a rebuild or an update needs few
calls. `sync` in the result says what was fetched: Garmin calls, .FIT files downloaded
(fitDownloads) and new activities.
`digest`, first in the result: the server's totals for the whole period and for each
Monday-Sunday week (sessions, km, hours, load), the training load of the last 7 and 28 days,
best efforts, races and strength top sets, the plan verdicts of the strength sessions done
(`strengthPlan`), the long runs with their half split and HR drift, the
longest run and the race predictions (Riegel), the page's readiness verdict for today with its
inputs (`readiness`), and today's fitness, fatigue and form (`fitnessFatigue`); quote them
instead of your own sums. For another date range, use the activities: each one is on its own
line. A load is null (n/a) when the sessions have none; estimatedLoads counts the loads that
are estimates from heart rate. A week with partial: true starts before the period. Without HRV
and sleep data the digest has no `readiness`: give the verdict as n/a.
The full result is large: 12 weeks can be about 180 KB, which can be over the tool output limit
of the assistant. `writeDashboard` with `preview: true` gives only the digest, the activities of
each board and the settings.

workouts.description: Also the laps of the runs of each run name that repeats, to compare a workout across weeks: the last 8 (downloaded once) and older ones whose .FIT file is saved; default false

recoveryHistory.description: Also the sleep and resting HR rows of the whole period, not only the last 14 days

name: getFitnessAge
description:
Garmin fitness age for a date, yyyy-MM-dd: fitnessAge, chronologicalAge, achievableFitnessAge
and previousFitnessAge, and components: bodyFat, vigorousDaysAvg and vigorousMinutesAvg (per
week) and rhr (resting HR), each with its value and, when Garmin suggests one, targetValue and
potentialAge (the fitness age at the target). stale is Garmin's flag for an old value. Use it
for fitness age; for the body fat trend use getWeight.

name: getHeartRateZones
description:
The heart rate zones set in Garmin Connect: a list with one entry per sport that has its own
zones (sport DEFAULT for the others), each with trainingMethod (how Garmin sets the zones),
zone1Floor to zone5Floor (the lowest bpm of each zone; a zone ends where the next one
starts, zone 5 at maxHeartRateUsed), maxHeartRateUsed, restingHeartRateUsed and
lactateThresholdHeartRateUsed. It takes no parameters. It gives the limits only: the time in
each zone of an activity is hrZonesSec in listActivities.

name: getHrvRange
description:
Overnight HRV for a date range, yyyy-MM-dd: hrvSummaries, one row per night with HRV data
(a night without data has no row), with calendarDate, lastNightAvg (ms, the average of the
night), lastNight5MinHigh, weeklyAvg (the 7-night average), status (BALANCED, UNBALANCED or
LOW) and baseline (balancedLow to balancedUpper: the normal range). Ask at most 28 days in
one call: Garmin may refuse a longer range. Use it for the HRV trend; for the sleep of a
night use getSleep, and for resting HR use getDailyHeartRate or getDailySummary.

name: getSleep
description:
Sleep for one night (date: the morning you woke up), or for up to 14 nights (fromDate and
toDate), yyyy-MM-dd, as one compact row per night: bedtime and wake (local HH:mm), hours of
sleep, deep, light, REM and awake, the sleep score and its quality, the sleep need (hours),
average heart rate, average and lowest SpO2, average respiration, awake count, average sleep
stress and Garmin's feedback. Missing values are left out, and a night without sleep data has
only its date. Set raw=true for Garmin's JSON.

raw.description: Return Garmin's raw JSON instead of the summary

name: getWeight
description:
Weight for a date range, yyyy-MM-dd: the latest weight of each day (with body fat, muscle
and bone mass, BMI and body water when a scale records them), the average of the range, and
the last weight before and the first after the range. Set includeAll=true for every entry
of each day. Weight, muscle mass and bone mass are in grams. The range has no day cap: ask a
trend of months in one call.

includeAll.description: Every weight entry of each day, not only the latest

name: listActivities
description:
List the user's Garmin activities (most recent first) as a compact summary: id, name, type,
local start time, distance (km), moving duration, average pace, average/max heart rate,
cadence, ascent; when Garmin has them: elapsed time (if longer than moving time), race flag,
Garmin training load, aerobic/anaerobic training effect and label, seconds in HR zones 1-5,
calories, moderate/vigorous intensity minutes, body battery change, steps, swim SWOLF, pool
length, lengths and strokes, power, mountain-bike grit and flow, running form (stride, ground
contact, vertical oscillation and ratio), grade-adjusted pace, best efforts (1k, mile, 5k,
10k, half, marathon) and run/walk segments. Dates are yyyy-MM-dd. Set raw=true for Garmin's
full JSON. limit is at most 200; names filters the last 200 activities of the date window.
Use it to find activity ids and to compare many activities. For the laps, sets or plan of one
activity, give its id to getActivityLaps, getActivitySets or getActivityWorkouts.

activityType.description: Activity type key (optional): a parent type such as running or cycling, or a subtype such as trail_running

raw.description: Return Garmin's raw JSON instead of the summary

names.description: Activity names (optional): keep only the activities whose name contains one of them, ignoring case

name: scheduleDashboardRefresh
description:
Turns on, changes or stops the automatic refresh of a dashboard page. Use it only when the user
asks for it or says yes to the question of a dashboard prompt. A job in the scheduler of the
computer (launchd, cron or Task Scheduler) replaces the data of the page at the given times, also
with no assistant open. The refresh removes the coach notes, because old notes do not agree
with new data. The computer must be on at that time. The page must exist (writeDashboard first).
`last` is the last automatic run: its time, the pages that it could not update, with the error,
and in `partial` the pages that it updated with gaps. A page shows a note when its update is
more than 1 hour late: `last` tells why.
`cron`: convert what the user says, in any language, into a 5-field cron expression in local
time: minute hour day-of-month month weekday, numbers only (0 = Sunday), e.g. "0 7 * * 1-5" for
weekdays at 7. Two runs must be at least 1 hour apart. The cron is for all scheduled pages;
`path` adds that page (default the main page); `off` stops the refresh of `path`, or of every
page when no `path` is given. Without arguments it only reads. The reply has `next`, the next
runs in local time: tell them to the user in their language, so they can check the schedule.

cron.description: minute hour day-of-month month weekday, e.g. "0 7 * * *"; default 0 7 * * *

path.description: The .html file; relative paths are inside the data dir

name: showDashboard
description:
Shows the training dashboard in the chat, in assistants that show MCP Apps: the page of `path`
(default <data-dir>/garmin-dashboard.html) with its layout, custom widgets, languages and settings,
or the preset page when there is none, with new data of the last `weeks` weeks. Writes nothing and
has no coach notes. Returns the page path, the digest of the data and the page settings. Other
assistants show only this reply: there, writeDashboard writes the page as a file.

weeks.description: Weeks to cover, default the page's or 12, max 52

path.description: The .html file; relative paths are inside the data dir

name: writeDashboard
description:
Writes the training dashboard page (default <data-dir>/garmin-dashboard.html) with the data of the
last `weeks` weeks, and returns its path and a short digest of the data (totals, weekly sums, load,
best efforts, races, long runs, race predictions, strength top sets, readiness, fitness and form,
HRV, recovery, fitness age, sync) for the coach notes. Without HRV and sleep data the digest has
no readiness: give the verdict as n/a.
An existing page keeps all its code, layout and widgets: its data is replaced. A page with
different page code gets the page code of the server and keeps its layout and widgets; the result then has `page: "upgraded"`,
`previousServer` (the server version that wrote the page, n/a when unknown) and `server`. Every page from the template
also gets the custom widgets of the widget library (<data-dir>/widgets.json), not placed on a board.
On a page from the template, an edited board also gets the widgets that a release adds to its preset, one time;
the result lists the ones that the page shows in `addedWidgets` (board -> widget ids).
`layout` writes a new page
from the template: `preset` (the default widgets) or `blank` (empty boards). It keeps the languages
added with editDashboard `languages`. `page` writes your own
page code instead; it must contain /* garmin-data:start */null/* garmin-data:end */. A replaced
page is kept as <file>.bak. The .bak keeps the page from before the build: a write that follows
within 15 minutes (the notes, a new title) does not replace it.
`notes`: at most 5 plain-text coach notes; the server escapes them.
`settings` replace the page's settings (title, headline, sports, data to leave out, languages,
themes); without them the page keeps its own. The page holds only the data, languages and themes
they keep. `pageLanguages` in the result lists the languages of the page's Language menu, and
`settings` the settings that the page keeps. `missingProfileLanguage` is the language of the Garmin
profile when the page has no texts in it (it shows English); editDashboard `languages` adds it.
`missingWidgetTexts` lists the custom widgets that miss texts in a language of the page, with
those languages; editDashboard `widgetTexts` adds them.
`preview: true` writes nothing: it returns the digest, the activities of each board and the
`settings` of the page.

notes.description: Coach notes, plain text; without notes the page has none

layout.description: Write a new page from the template with this layout

page.description: Your own page code, with an empty garmin-data block, instead of the template

path.description: The .html file; relative paths are inside the data dir

title.description: Replaces the title in every language

sports.description: The boards to keep, e.g. running, cycling; all when not set

exclude.description: The data to leave out of the page

languages.description: Languages to keep: en, it, de, fr, es, pt; when not set, English and the language of the Garmin profile

language.description: Default language: auto or a code

themes.description: Themes to keep: system, midnight, graphite, ocean, forest, plum, munichDark, light, paper, mist, munich, hcDark, hcLight

workouts.description: Compare the same run workout across weeks (Workout trend widget): the server loads the laps of the last 8 sessions of each repeated run name, and of older ones whose .FIT file is saved; off when not set

recoveryHistory.description: Keep the sleep and resting HR rows of the whole period in the page, not only the last 14 days; off when not set

settings.description: The page settings; replaces the page's own

preview.description: Write nothing: return the digest, the activities of each board and the page settings
